title: Tiered Preemption + Graceful Handoff for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Problem: During capacity contention we have three frequent failure modes: abrupt evictions causing user-visible errors, unfair preemption of long-lived sessions, and cascading cold-start latency when workloads are migrated. This PRD proposes a Tiered Preemption and Graceful Handoff system for Dedicated capacity that minimizes customer disruption while preserving strong isolation for reserved tenants.

Core idea: Introduce an admission + preemption controller that assigns runtime slots to priority tiers, issues a soft-preempt signal with a configurable grace window, and orchestrates handoff flows (model downgrade, regional failover, or queued warm-up) to avoid hard evictions. The controller is integrated with the existing reservation ledger, autoscaler, and routing/fallback policies so we can preempt with policy-aware reasoning (cost vs latency vs SLA class).

Scope: MVP covers the scheduling/controller behavior, API surface for tenant-level priority/config, runtime soft-preempt hooks (SDK and API response flags), metrics and dashboards, and a canary rollout plan. Out of scope for MVP: per-token billing changes, new KMS flows, and advanced ML model conversion for warmdown (these are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: When dedicated pool utilization reaches configurable threshold, controller demotes low-priority queued requests and issues soft-preempt notices instead of immediate evictions
Soft-preempt notice is sent via API streaming and server-sent event hooks; client SDK receives a "PREEMPT_NOTICE" event with recommended fallback within 2s of decision

Handoff options: (1) fallback to smaller/quantized model, (2) route to secondary region with documented latency delta, or (3) enqueue with guaranteed prewarm token. At least one handoff option is executed successfully for 95% of soft-preempted sessions in integration tests
No customer-facing 5xx errors attributable to hard-evictions in canary region during 24h contention test (compared to baseline)
Telemetry exposes per-tenant preempt_count, preempt_latency_delta, handoff_success_rate, and average grace_window used
Policy controls in Console: per-tenant priority tier, max preemptions per hour, and minimum guaranteed slots must be editable and persist via API
E2E load tests show high-priority responder latency SLO (p50/p95/p99) remains within existing SLA during controlled contention runs
Documentation (Confluence), SDK change log, and migration guide published prior to beta rollout
success_metrics: Reduce hard-eviction incidents for reserved tenants by >= 60% within 8 weeks of rollout
Decrease cold-start tail latency (p99) after handoff by >= 30% vs current hard-eviction fallback
Achieve handoff_success_rate >= 95% in synthetic multi-tenant stress tests
Maintain high-priority request success rate >= 99.9% during 95th percentile contention events
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Complexity of controller could introduce regression bugs in scheduler. Mitigation: Start with simplified admission rules, comprehensive unit tests, and staged rollout (canary -> beta -> global)
Risk: Fairness concerns from customers demoted by preemption. Mitigation: Expose full audit logs, per-tenant metrics, and opt-in grace credits (customers can purchase burst credits)
Risk: SDK adoption lag causing poor handoff behavior. Mitigation: Provide server-side fallbacks that are safe if SDK does not implement PREEMPT_NOTICE, plus a clear deprecation migration plan
Risk: Increased cross-region egress/costs during handoff. Mitigation: Telemetry and quota guards; tie handoff policies to billing alerts and admin consent
rollout_plan: Dark launch: Deploy controller in read-only mode to collect decisions (no enforced preemption) in staging and canary zones (2 weeks)
Canary: Enable soft-preempt enforcement for <5% of traffic on a selected customer subset; monitor handoff_success_rate and error budget (2 weeks)
Beta: Expand to opt-in customers with dedicated SLAs and provide migration support (4 weeks)
GA: Default-on for new reservations; existing customers get 30-day notice and UI migration tool (6 weeks after beta)
